title: Bhature
description: Bhature are fluffy, soft, and lightly crisp deep-fried Indian breads made from refined flour, semolina, yogurt, and a leavening mixture. Traditionally served hot with chole, they are a popular North Indian favorite.

ingredients.title: For the Bhatura Dough
items: Warm water – approximately ½ cup, or as needed

instruction.title: Step 1 – Mixing the Dry Ingredients
steps: Sift the all-purpose flour, semolina, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt together in a large bowl.
Mix thoroughly to distribute the ingredients evenly.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Adding Yogurt and Oil
steps: Add the yogurt and oil or melted ghee to the dry ingredients.
Mix with your fingers or a spoon until the mixture becomes crumbly and well combined.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Kneading the Dough
steps: Gradually add warm water a little at a time while kneading.
Knead until a smooth, soft, and slightly sticky dough forms.
The dough should be softer than regular chapati dough.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Resting the Dough
steps: Cover the dough with a damp cloth.
Let it rest for at least 2 hours at room temperature.
This resting and fermentation period helps give the bhature their characteristic softness and puffiness.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Dividing and Rolling
steps: After resting, knead the dough briefly.
Divide it into equal-sized lemon-sized balls.
Roll each ball into a smooth round disc about 5–6 inches in diameter.
Use minimal flour for dusting while rolling.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Heating the Oil
steps: Heat oil in a deep frying pan or wok over medium-high heat.
The oil should be hot but not smoking.
Test the temperature by dropping in a small piece of dough; it should rise immediately.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Frying the Bhature
steps: Carefully slide a rolled dough disc into the hot oil.
Press gently with a slotted spoon to encourage the bhatura to puff.
Fry until golden brown on one side, then flip and fry the other side until golden and cooked through.
Remove with a slotted spoon.

instruction.title: Step 8 – Draining and Serving
steps: Drain excess oil from the bhatura on paper towels.
Serve hot with chole or your favorite curry.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with traditional chole (chickpea curry).
Pair with other North Indian curries for a hearty meal.
Enjoy immediately after frying for the best puffiness and texture.

chefTips: Resting the dough is essential for soft, fluffy, and puffy bhature.
Use fresh yogurt to support the fermentation and softness of the dough.
Keep the frying oil at a consistent temperature; oil that is too hot can burn the bhature, while oil that is too cool can make them greasy.
Press gently on the bhatura with a slotted spoon after adding it to the oil to encourage even puffing.
Keep the dough softer than regular chapati dough for a lighter final texture.
